chunks: Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about the sun: how it comes to a stillness every day, while on Friday there is no stillness for it. He said:
"Because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made Friday the most constricted of the days."
Then it was said to him: And why did He make it the most constricted of the days? He said: "Because on that day He does not punish the polytheists, due to its sanctity with Him."

key_terms.أَضْيَقَ اَلْأَيَّامِ: the most constricted of the days, indicating a special condition or status
key_terms.اَلشَّمْسِ: the sun, discussed here in relation to its daily stillness
key_terms.اَلْمُشْرِكِينَ: the polytheists, whose punishment is withheld on that day
key_terms.تَرْكُدُ: comes to a stillness or pause
key_terms.يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ: Friday, the day singled out in the hadith

ai.seo_question: Why does the sun not have its daily stillness on Friday according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a cosmological distinction for Friday, presenting it as a day with a unique sanctity before Allah. It explains that the sun does not undergo its usual daily stillness on Friday because of the special status of that day, during which punishment of the polytheists is withheld.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.676 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) was asked about the sun’s stillness (or 'pause') every day and why there is no such stillness for it on Jumu’ah.
Imam (as) said: "Because Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, made Jumu’ah the most constricted (or significant) of the days."
It was then asked: "And why did He make it the most constricted of days?"
Imam (as) said: "Because on that day He does not punish the polytheists, due to the sanctity it holds with Him."
